paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: : labelformat=parens, labelsep=period
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the performance of AlphaEdit and DeltaEdit methods on GPT2-XL, comparing their top efficacy (Efficacy_top) and associated noise (noise_E) as a function of an unlabeled x-axis ranging from 0 to 3000 in increments of 500. The x-axis is linear and has no units specified. The left y-axis, labeled "Efficacy_top", ranges from 86 to 100 with a linear scale and tick marks every 2 units. The right y-axis, labeled "noise_E", ranges from 2 to 12 with a linear scale and tick marks every 2 units. The AlphaEdit Efficacy_top is represented by a dashed red line with square markers, starting at approximately 99.5 at x=0 and decreasing to about 86.5 at x=3000. The AlphaEdit noise_E is shown as a solid red line with circular markers, starting at approximately 2.5 at x=0 and increasing to about 11.5 at x=3000. The DeltaEdit Efficacy_top is depicted as a dashed purple line with square markers, beginning at approximately 99.5 at x=0 and declining to around 94 at x=3000. The DeltaEdit noise_E is shown as a solid purple line with circular markers, starting at approximately 2.5 at x=0 and rising to about 11 at x=3000. The two efficacy curves (dashed lines) are nearly identical at the start and decrease steadily, while the two noise curves (solid lines) increase steadily and are nearly parallel, with DeltaEdit noise_E slightly lower than AlphaEdit noise_E across the range.
